To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the allocation of coproductions by multistep processes to unit processes can respect the material, energy, financial, and production balances of the original data set only if all unit processes are multistep processes and all multistep processes are coproductions.

the following modeling families are balanced: (1) allocation of a single output to a single unit process, (2) allocation of a multifunctional unit process to a single output, (3) constructs with single inputs and outputs, (4) constructs with single multifunctional unit processes, (5) constructs with multiple inputs and outputs, and (6) allocation to a single unit processes of multiple outputs of a multifunctionality.

the necessary and sufficient condition for allocations to simultaneously respect material, energy, financial, and production balances is that they are applied to a single product, single process inventory table, and the same is true for constructs if the inventory is a supply and use table.
